discovery: Theoretical discovery of anyons: fractional quantum statistics in two dimensions

nominees.name: Jan Myrheim
nominees.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Trondheim, Norway

subfield: Condensed matter theory / topological quantum matter
motivation: In 1977 Leinaas and Myrheim showed, from the topology of configuration space for identical particles, that in two dimensions quantum statistics need not be bosonic or fermionic: exchange can produce any phase. In 1982 Wilczek independently gave these particles a concrete realization as charge-flux composites and named them anyons. This idea, once considered a mathematical curiosity, became the conceptual basis for understanding fractionally charged quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect, for topological order, and for non-Abelian anyons, which underpin proposals for topological quantum computation. The 2020 experiments by groups in Paris and Purdue, using anyon collisions and Fabry-Perot interferometry, directly observed fractional braiding statistics, and later experiments in quantum Hall and moire systems have confirmed it further. The work changed how physicists understand identical particles. It is now a basic principle of quantum mechanics, taught alongside the spin-statistics theorem.
